text:
Colorado's 6-1 win at Ball Arena was lopsided on the scoreboard and fairly earned on the ice, but the margin got a push from a Manson goal that had a 2% chance of going in. The Avalanche carried 3.59 expected goals to St. Louis's 1.97 and a 76% share of deserved wins, so the better team won. It just didn't win by five.

The first period set the terms. Colorado out-chanced the Blues 1.53 to 0.43 in expected goals, with Cale Makar and Martin Necas scoring at 4:09 and 13:12. The second period turned it into a rout. Josh Manson's snap shot at 5:38, the lowest-percentage look of the night, made it 3-0, and Artturi Lehkonen added a fourth at 11:40. Nicolas Roy and Necas then scored 23 seconds apart late in the period, at 18:02 and 18:25, to make it 6-0. Necas finished with two goals and an assist, and Nathan MacKinnon had three assists. Necas and MacKinnon each had more than 1.6 expected goals for on the ice with under 0.4 against.

Jordan Binnington faced 36 shots and allowed 6 on 3.59 expected, giving up 2.41 goals more than the chances warranted. The Blues played the third period on better terms, out-chancing Colorado 1.04 to 1.10 in expected goals, and Dalibor Dvorsky's backhand at 2:34 ended Mackenzie Blackwood's shutout bid. Blackwood stopped 25 of 26, including a 26% chance from Dylan Holloway.
